=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached singly at different nodes along the stem, as seen in images 1, 2, and 3)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are concentrated at the terminal end of the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves consist of a single blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins appear smooth and continuous)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaf is broadest in the middle and tapers toward both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tip comes to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf base tapers to a wedge shape where it meets the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible and distinct (veins are clearly visible as depressed lines on the leaf surface)

    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are relatively short compared to the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears rigid and lignified, consistent with a tree seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the stem)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is green with some brownish discoloration near the base)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem appears relatively smooth without prominent ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
